question: Should OpenClaw support first-party per-agent restore/clone, and what credential, transcript, and overwrite policy is allowed for `--agent` and `--as`?
rationale: The implementation would copy or rewrite sensitive auth state, session history, workspaces, SQLite state, and config entries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent security and product contract.

options.title: Approve Scoped Core Design
options.body: Define a local per-agent archive/restore contract with dry-run, manifest validation, safe extraction, credential/session portability rules, config rewrite rules, rollback, tests, and docs before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Backup Umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue open but settle the archive format and destructive restore semantics under the broader native backup lifecycle first.

options.title: Defer Native Clone
options.body: Document manual recovery and leave optional sync/cloud clone workflows to plugins until maintainers decide the core restore API boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped Core Design
recommendation.body: Define a local per-agent archive/restore contract with dry-run, manifest validation, safe extraction, credential/session portability rules, config rewrite rules, rollback, tests, and docs before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior review routing and recent backup-area history make this the best observed person to sponsor or reject the product/security boundary decision.
